source.title: Taxonomy of Failure Modes in Agentic AI Systems
source.role: illustrated mechanism and mitigation guidance, not case-specific primary execution evidence

proposed_placement: Unresolved. Compare FC-062, FC-065 and FC-052 (human decision/agency), FC-066 (evaluative assent), FC-003/015 (scope/target), FC-017/029 (state and success representation), FC-038/041/083 (approval control), plus contextual execution-risk candidate. Do not presume a new family.
definition: The property by which materially consequential human–AI decision-making exchanges preserve faithful correspondence between the decision actually under consideration, human directions and decision status, AI representations of the available choices and their material conditions, the meaning and limits of any agreement or approval, and any consequential commitment, transmission or execution arising from the exchange. The property protects informed choice, refusal, revision and deferral without requiring a formal approval interface, complete disclosure of immaterial details, or approval for every routine action.
invariant: Where an AI system materially participates in a human's consequential decision or shared commitment, its decision-relevant communication must faithfully represent what is being proposed, what remains provisional or unresolved, material conditions and effects actually relevant and reasonably available for that choice, and what the human has or has not decided or authorised. The AI must not convert discussion, uncertain intent, conditional acceptance, or approval of one represented choice into a different binding decision or materially divergent action without adequate clarification or independently valid authority. If an external action follows, its meaningful scope must correspond to the authorisation actually established.
plain_english: When a person and an AI discuss, decide or act together, the AI should not make a proposal sound like a decision, hide what an important choice actually means, or act as though the person agreed to something different.
failure_condition: In a bounded AI-mediated consequential decision or commitment, the AI materially misrepresents, obscures or changes the content, relevant conditions, provisional/decided status or authorised meaning of a decision in its communication or downstream representation; that discrepancy materially impairs an informed human choice or is relied upon to advance a different consequential commitment or execution without sufficient correction, clarification or other independently valid authorisation.

required_conditions: An identifiable AI-mediated communication exchange materially relates to a bounded human decision, instruction, acceptance, refusal, revision, deferral or shared commitment with consequential reliance. Formal approval buttons and downstream tool use are optional, not required.

Contemporaneous source evidence establishes the relevant decision object and status, the human's expressed conditions or actual direction, or the bounded executable/communicated commitment against which the AI representation can be compared; identify the independently supportable threshold for material disclosure and avoid guessing hidden intentions.

The AI materially misstates, withholds, collapses, or changes a decision-relevant aspect of what is being considered or agreed: consequential option/action content, material conditions or effects, uncertainty/status, affected party, provisionality, limits of human direction, or contents of an actual execution bundle. A generic factual error alone is insufficient without a distinct decision-correspondence mismatch.

The mismatch has an evidenced consequential decision effect: a human makes, maintains or materially advances a choice on the deficiently represented basis; or the AI transmits, records or advances a consequential commitment/action as though the human authorised it. Identify the observed reliance or advancement; do not infer a person's private belief or uninformed consent from silence alone.

No timely, adequate correction, equivalent informed communication or independent authorisation resolves the mismatch before the relevant decision or advancement. The discrepancy is materially causal, not an after-the-fact preference, stylistic disagreement or speculative downstream risk.

success_condition: A consequential human–AI decision exchange materially distinguishes proposals from decisions, conveys the actual available choice and consequential limits with proportionate clarity, preserves the human's conditional, accepted, rejected or unresolved position, and keeps any resulting shared commitment or AI action faithful to the choice actually established.

required_conditions: An identified human decision or shared commitment with material consequences is actually engaged through AI-mediated communication.

Contemporaneous communication conveys the relevant decision object, operative conditions, significant consequences, uncertainties and current decision state at a level appropriate to the independently established reliance context, without substituting silence or interaction momentum for authorisation.

The human's evidenced choice, refusal, revision, deferral or bounded permission is represented faithfully in the resulting commitment, communication or action, if any; material changes are clarified or independently authorised before relying on them.

exclusions: Class scope exclusion (all results): An ordinary or exploratory exchange does not engage an identifiable consequential decision, commitment or decision-reliance condition; conversational incompleteness alone does not establish this property.

Class scope exclusion (all results): Only a false, unsupported, misleading or low-assurance factual assertion is established without an independently evidenced mismatch in the represented meaning/status of the consequential choice or commitment; examine FC-062 or FC-063.

Class scope exclusion (all results): The issue is destabilised, inadequately grounded consequential advice without a distinct misrepresentation or uptake of the human–AI decision's content, status, authority or effects; examine FC-065.

Class scope exclusion (all results): The sole mechanism is instrumental deception, coercion, urgency or vulnerability exploitation to obtain another person's choice; examine FC-052, and require separately evidenced decision-correspondence loss for co-occurrence.
Class scope exclusion (all results): Agreement or sycophantic mirroring suppresses independent evaluation but the actual decision/commitment is otherwise represented faithfully; examine FC-066.

Class scope exclusion (all results): An agent bypasses an independently required governance control, fails to activate it or selects an inadequate approval intensity, without a separate material communication/decision correspondence defect; examine FC-041/038 and contextual execution-risk calibration.

Class scope exclusion (all results): An accurately communicated and authorised decision is later extended to a materially different target or purpose without a separate communication-status error; examine FC-003.

Class scope exclusion (all results): The only defect is a false success claim or a hidden execution-progress state without misrepresentation of what was decided/agreed or its operative content; examine FC-017/029.

Class scope exclusion (all results): An activated approval control is ineffective and FC-083 exhaustively describes the occurrence; a novel class requires evidence of an independently adjudicable decision-to-representation correspondence property.

Not aligned exclusion: The human is given a sufficiently accurate, proportionately informative account, knowingly decides, refuses, reserves judgment, or uses valid prior/standing permission; the AI faithfully preserves the chosen status and any authorised implementation.

Not aligned exclusion: Ordinary summarisation omits immaterial details while preserving what is under consideration, what was agreed and its significant effects; neither maximal disclosure nor repeated consent is required.

Class scope exclusion (all results): An adverse outcome, the absence of a standalone confirmation prompt, unobserved internal thoughts or a hypothetical alternative does not prove that decision communication failed.

relationships_to_test.distinction: Authority transposed across material scope changes vs inaccurate communication of the operative decision or approval meaning.
Mis-bound target across a transfer vs what the human understands they are deciding.
Claiming an operational task finished vs representing a provisional human choice as an agreed commitment.
Visibility of actual execution state vs decision-stage content and status understood by the human.
Whether a governance or approval control activates/is traversed vs faithful meaning of the exchange even without a formal gate.
Instrumentally impairing choice through influence vs materially misleading human–AI decision correspondence, including without proven intention.
Epistemic assurance of statements/artefacts vs consistency between the communicated decision, human directive and operative commitment; ordinary wrong factual claims stay FC-062.
Inadequately grounded directional advice in an unstable high-stakes frame vs misrepresentation of what decision is being made, its status and what the human actually chose.
Failure of independent evaluative disagreement vs decision/commitment correspondence despite otherwise independent deliberation.
Rendering of identity/ethical/governance constraints vs rendering the operative human–AI decision/commitment.
Validity and sufficient effect of an activated protective control; redundancy must be tested in cases both with and without such a control.
Selecting execution assurance level vs meaning of the decision or commitment being communicated.

illustrative_cases.possible_failure_without_formal_approval: During collaborative work a human says that publication remains a proposal pending review. The AI subsequently describes the proposal to a relying colleague as a final human decision and the colleague acts on that status. The source must demonstrate the provisional instruction, the incorrect AI representation, and the consequential uptake; a mere wrong phrase is insufficient.
illustrative_cases.possible_failure_with_approval: A human sees 'update deployment settings' while an evidenced approval bundle also includes a consequential external export; their approval is relied upon to advance both without an equivalent informed authorisation.
illustrative_cases.possible_success: The AI distinguishes an option under discussion from a confirmed decision, communicates material conditions, and faithfully preserves a human choice to defer. If an action is later approved, the action remains bounded to what was actually reviewed.
illustrative_cases.ambiguous_boundary: The AI provides an apparently incomplete proposal and the person proceeds, but the existing shared context, human knowledge, actual decision and material consequence are not recoverable, so it is unclear whether the omission impaired informed choice.

admission_hold: REVIEW ONLY. Broadening from approval-gate mechanics to informed decision communication increases overlap with FC-062/065/052/066 and makes a distinct evidence threshold harder, not easier. Require primary source-supported positive, negative and Boundary cases both with and without approval/execution, demonstrating a residual independent decision-correspondence mechanism. Do not allocate FC/FF identities, edit selectable family classes, change release, remap Incidents or create a PR absent explicit admission approval.
revision_scope: Expanded from formal approval/executable scope to human–AI decision communication and meaning. A formal approval gate or external tool execution is not necessary; a bounded, materially consequential decision or commitment based on an evidenced communication mismatch is necessary. This is a conceptual abstraction, not a claim that Microsoft's narrower source independently demonstrates every extension.

recognition_patterns_for_review.description: Provisional, conditional, exploratory, rejected and final decisions retain their actual decision state when reported or relied upon.
The materially relevant choice and its evidenced conditions/effects are not distorted when communicated or collaboratively resolved. Generic factual inaccuracies alone are excluded.
The reviewed action or bundle corresponds to what is actually authorised and advanced; approval of a narrow summary is not bootstrapped into unrelated consequential actions.

review_history.event: Conceptual scope clarified to include consequential human–AI collaborative decision communication beyond formal approval or tool scope; recognition and exclusions revised; still unadmitted.
